Split the conjunction and prove both parts by monotonicity.

- For `IntegrationParams.toFilteriUnion`, view the filter as an indexed union/supremum of filters determined by admissible tagged prepartitions. The inequality `l₁ ≤ l₂` relaxes the integration-parameter constraints, so every index admissible for `l₁` remains admissible for `l₂`. Reduce the goal to monotonicity of the indexed filter union, likely via an existing `toFilteriUnion_mono` lemma.

- For `nhdsSetWithin`, use its representation as the supremum of `nhdsWithin x t` over `x ∈ s`. Since `s ⊆ s'`, the supremum indexed by `s` is bounded by the one indexed by `s'`. Equivalently, apply the standard monotonicity lemma for `nhdsSetWithin` in its set argument.

The common mechanism is monotonicity of a filter-valued construction under enlargement of its indexing set.
